target_customer: Urban consumers in Mexico ordering groceries and daily essentials for delivery in about 20 minutes
problem: Grocery delivery in Latin American cities was slow and expensive compared with fast dark-store models like Gopuff.
business_model: Consumer quick-commerce delivery from micro fulfillment centers (dark stores) with margin on goods and delivery fees

founders.name: Luis Mario Garcia
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he designed the software, ran warehouses, launched cities and personally delivered 1,000 orders.

founders.name: Javier Gonzalez
previous_startups: First company with an app that reached 500,000 users, per YC bio
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he has coded since age 12.

competitors.name: Rappi
competitors.traction_then: Already operating in Mexico per TechCrunch

competitors.name: Cornershop
competitors.what: Chilean grocery delivery marketplace acquired by Uber in 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: App and ordering software are standard; the hard parts were operational (inventory, dark stores, courier logistics).

defensibility.rationale: Delivery speed and prices were easy to match and required heavy capital; no moat documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A June 2022 Forbes report said Merqueo left Mexico amid competition from Rappi, Cornershop, Jokr, Orchata, Walmart and Jüsto, and Jokr exited Mexico in December 2021 per a Forbes Mexico headline.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Aug 2021) said Orchata launched about four months earlier, was in two Mexican cities, processing thousands of orders and growing 100 percent monthly, amid a quick-commerce boom.

branding.domain_note: Uses orchata.com (not horchata); no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as the Gopuff for Latin America

branding.community_and_virality: Press from TechCrunch, Enter.co and LAVCA; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press and a clear Gopuff pitch but no evidence of consumer brand pull; spelling differs from the drink horchata.

outcome_analysis: Orchata raised a 4M dollar seed in August 2021 after four months of operating, claiming 100 percent monthly growth in two cities, then went inactive. No post-mortem or shutdown report was found, so the cause is not public. Mexican quick commerce was crowded and capital hungry (Jokr exited in December 2021, Merqueo in 2022, Jüsto in 2025), so the failure labels are judgments from the market, not stated causes.
notes: The seed is confirmed by TechCrunch, LAVCA and Enter.co. The 2023-03-31 CB Insights round (labelled Seed VC-II) has no amount and rests on a single database; CB Insights totals 4.13M over four rounds. VCBacked labels Orchata pre-seed, a conflict. Competitor sources are dated August 2021, a year after the Summer 2020 batch, so treat as later; Rappi and Cornershop existed earlier (Cornershop acquired by Uber in 2019). The YC page has no launch post. The company site orchata.com returned HTTP 402. YC lists the batch as Winter 2020 while TechCrunch says Summer 2020; the queue says Winter 2020. Revenue claim of 6.3M and 30K customers is from the founder's YC bio only.
